tldr: Latent Space's Oct 7 newsletter put Claude Haiku 5.5 ahead of GPT-6 Luna at the same pricing. On Oct 20, Google Cloud added Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 to its Antigravity coding tool.
whats_new: R&D World compares Kimi K3.1 Pro against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra (Oct 23); only the headline is in the item, so the results are not confirmed here.
why_it_matters: Claude 5.5 models are reaching more surfaces (Antigravity), and a Chinese open-weight lab is now being benchmarked against Opus 5.5, so model-routing choices are being re-opened.

status.detail: Claude 5.5 models are spreading to new platforms while Kimi K3.1 Pro is being compared against them; no outcome is confirmed in these items.

beats.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 billed as better than GPT-6 Luna at the same price
beats.summary: A newsletter headline claim; the item carries no benchmark detail.

beats.headline: Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 land in Google Antigravity
beats.summary: Google Cloud offers both models inside Antigravity so developers can pick a model per task.

beats.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro compared with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra
beats.summary: R&D World frames a head-to-head; a third-party comparison, not an official source.

open_questions: Does the Kimi K3.1 Pro comparison show it matching Opus 5.5 on coding or agent tasks?
Is Kimi K3.1 Pro available via a public API, and at what price?
Do independent evals confirm Haiku 5.5 beating GPT-6 Luna at equal pricing?
take_for_builders: If you route between models, rerun your own evals with Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3.1 Pro as candidates before changing defaults, and treat the Haiku 5.5 vs Luna claim as unverified until you test it.
